big_case.notes: Emergency application over whether party-coordinated and joint-fundraising ad buys get the statutory lowest-unit-charge rate for the 60-day general-election window opening 2026-09-04, on a divided Fourth Circuit judgment (Wilkinson, J., dissenting) that set aside FCC Media Bureau guidance while the full Commission's review was pending; the FCC and United States were respondents defending the notice below. Tens of millions in party ad spending and both national party apparatuses' midterm strategy turned on it within days, and it sits atop the Court's June 2026 NRSC v. FEC coordinated-expenditure ruling — high political and financial stakes, but the legal question is a narrow finality/agency-action hook plus a §315(b) reading, and the vehicle is a stay pending certiorari rather than a merits judgment. Read formed from the record's application text and the outcome before weighing the candidates' own scores, which were unavoidably visible in the staged prediction.json.
